response.content:
## Companies Launched in Germany in 2026

The question is very broad — Germany saw a significant wave of new business formations in 2026. Here is an overview of the landscape along with notable examples:

### Overall Business Formation Trends

According to the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), approximately **103,700 businesses of greater economic significance** were founded in Germany during the first three quarters of 2026, representing a **4.5% increase** compared to the same period a year earlier. Total business start-ups reached about **525,100** in the first three quarters, up **7.7% year on year**.

### Notable Startups and Companies Active/Launched in 2026

Germany's startup ecosystem in 2026 has been dominated by **deeptech and defence** themes, with VCs pouring significant capital into the space. Some of the most prominent German startups raising major rounds in 2026 include:

- **Helsing** (Munich) — AI-based defence technology; raised €1.6B in a Series E+ round (Jul 2026)
- **Neura Robotics** (Metzingen) — Robotics; raised €1.2B in a Series C (Jun 2026)
- **Quantum Systems** (Munich) — Defence drones; raised €1B in a Series D (Jul 2026)
- **Agile Robots** (Munich) — AI-powered industrial robotics; raised $500M Series F at an $8.5B valuation (Nov 2026), backed by SoftBank and Nvidia
- **Stark** (Berlin) — Defence technology/drone systems; raised €500M (Jun 2026)
- **Proxima Fusion** (Munich) — Fusion energy/clean energy; raised €411M (Jul 2026)
- **The Exploration Company** (Gauting) — Space; raised €387.2M Series C (Sep 2026)
- **Parloa** (Berlin) — AI; raised €350M Series D (Jan 2026)
- **Cloover** (Berlin) — Clean energy; raised €1.2B Series A (Jan 2026)
- **maincubes** (Frankfurt am Main) — Data centres; raised €2.5B (Jan 2026)
- **VÆRIDION** (Germany) — Electric regional aviation
- **Hypersonica** (Germany) — Sovereign hypersonic deep-strike systems; secured €100M
- **NeuralSat** (Germany) — High-speed data network in space; raised €2.9M
- **Marble Cognition** (Munich) — AI coworkers for business process automation; raised €3.35M

### "Made for Germany" Initiative

A notable development in 2026 was the **"Made for Germany" initiative**, launched by **61 companies** that collectively pledged **€631 billion** in investments toward Germany's economic growth by 2028, covering capital expenditures, R&D spending, and contributions from international investors. The initiative focuses on digitisation, innovation, infrastructure, sustainability, and skilled labour.

### Smaller Companies Founded in 2026

Among smaller firms, examples include:
- **Closerplatform** (Bremen) — Sales outsourcing and business consulting, established in 2026

Many more small and medium-sized enterprises were founded across sectors including AI, cybersecurity, logistics, software development, and clean energy throughout the year.

---

A comprehensive list of every company launched in Germany in 2026 is not available in a single source, given the scale (hundreds of thousands of new registrations). The examples above highlight the most prominent and well-funded new ventures and initiatives of the year.

At the same time, the number of complete closures of businesses of greater economic significance fell 2.4 percent to about 72,500, Destatis said.

# Tech Giants Invest in German Robotics Start-Up at $8.5 Billion Valuation

Agile Robots plans to expand in the United States and increase production in Europe after raising funds in a round led by SoftBank.

Agile Robots, a German company developing industrial robots powered by artificial intelligence, has raised $500 million in new funding from investors including SoftBank and Nvidia that values the start-up at $8.5 billion.

The investment will allow Agile to expand in the United States, increase production in Germany and move into new markets — ahead of a potential future initial public offering, said Zhaopeng Chen, Agile’s founder. The company is working with partners including Google DeepMind and has raised a total of $2 billion. [...] Agile is among a crop of fast-growing companies combining artificial intelligence and robotics to help factories increase productivity and lower costs. Developing humanoids and other robots that can carry out more complex tasks in the physical world is critical in Europe, which is trying to narrow an A.I. gap with the United States and China and revive its struggling industries.

“Physical A.I. is one of the solutions for Europe,” said Mr. Chen, who started the company in Germany in 2018 after studying engineering in China and completing his doctorate at the German Aerospace Center. [...] Agile’s valuation puts the start-up on par with European companies including Quantum Systems, the German defense technology company valued at $8 billion in July, and Wayve, the British autonomous driving company valued at $8.6 billion in February. Neura Robotics, a German company that has raised funds from companies including Nvidia, Amazon and the cryptocurrency company Tether, was valued at about $7 billion after raising as much as $1.4 billion.
